summary: Frail 86-year-old man (CFS 7, ASA III) with a reducible minimally symptomatic inguinal hernia: watchful waiting rather than elective repair.

inputs.hpi: Several months of a right groin lump on standing that goes back lying down; mild ache only; never stuck. Lives with his daughter; mobilises with a frame; needs help with bathing.

exam.abdomen: Reducible right inguinal hernia with a cough impulse, controlled at the deep ring. Left groin normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right inguinal hernia, reducible, minimally symptomatic
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Reducible right inguinal hernia, minimally symptomatic, in a frail 86-year-old (CFS 7).

match: re:observe rather than elective inguinal hernia repair: watchful waiting

guideline.name: CPOC/BGS perioperative care for people living with frailty

rationale: Watchful waiting is safe for minimally symptomatic inguinal hernias in men (Fitzgibbons 2006; O'Dwyer 2006); severe frailty raises operative harm, so the balance favours observation (HerniaSurge 2018; CPOC 2021).
